title: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

sections.label: UN General Assembly pandemic multilateralism
sections.summary: Assembly President Bozkir said the pandemic showed multilateral cooperation is key and stressed collective action and vaccine multilateralism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In closing the 75th session of the UN General Assembly last September, Assembly President Volkan Bozkir noted that the pandemic has been a test, demonstrating that multilateral cooperation is the key to overcoming global challenges, and he stressed the need for collective action to tackle common threats and “vaccine multilateralism” to combat the coronavirus.

sections.label: Singaporeans home, supply chains, COVAX
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister about bringing Singaporeans home, keeping supply chains connected, and Singapore's role in COVAX.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Can the Minister, therefore, speak on our efforts to bring Singaporeans home over the course of the pandemic as borders closed?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: How did the Ministry do its part to ensure that our supply chain continuously connected us to the world?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As we begin our vaccination campaign in earnest, it is worthwhile stating that Singapore is an early supporter of COVAX, the COVID-19 Vaccination Global Access initiative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: How is Singapore playing its role as a responsible global partner and neighbour in this regard?

sections.label: Singapore's US$5 million COVAX contribution
sections.summary: It asks how Singapore's US$5 million COVAX AMC contribution was determined, how it compares, and whether it can go to ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In December last year, Singapore announced a contribution of US$5 million to the COVAX Advanced Market Commitment or AMC financing instrument.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: How was this contribution sum of US$5 million determined and how does it compare with the contributions of other nations?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The current US administration is committing up to US$4 billion to the facility and G7 leaders have just issued statement calling for all partners to increase support for COVAX.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With ASEAN centrality in mind, has Singapore avail itself of this option so that it can channel parts of this donation to ASEAN countries?

sections.label: Discouraging vaccine hoarding
sections.summary: It asks how friends of the COVAX Facility can help discourage vaccine hoarding, especially by richer developed countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Most specifically, how can the friends of COVAX Facility help discourage vaccine hoarding, especially by the richer developed countries?

sections.label: Singapore vaccination capacity by year-end
sections.summary: MOH assessed Singapore can vaccinate its entire population by the end of the year if vaccine batches arrive as planned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As MOH had assessed, Singapore has the capacity and capability to vaccinate our entire population by the end of the year at the latest, if all our vaccine batches continue to arrive as planned.

sections.label: COVAX Facility objective and access
sections.summary: The COVAX Facility aims to obtain and distribute two billion COVID-19 vaccine doses equitably by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The objective of the COVAX Facility is to obtain and distribute two billion doses of COVID-19 vaccines equitably by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It will help people in low and lower middle income countries have access to COVID-19 vaccines.

sections.label: Vaccine distribution inequality
sections.summary: Vaccines are an important weapon against the virus, but 10 countries including Singapore have administered 75% of all vaccines while 130 countries have no doses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In the current pandemic, vaccines have become an important weapon against the virus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: But just 10 countries, including Singapore, have administered 75% of all vaccines, and 130 countries have no doses at all.

sections.label: Paris Agreement carbon targets
sections.summary: The Paris Agreement stated all parties will reduce their carbon footprint by more than 50% by 2030 and eliminate it by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Paris Agreement stated that that all parties will reduce their carbon footprint by more than 50% by 2030 and eliminate it by 2050.

sections.label: Digital data flow regulations
sections.summary: The pandemic has accelerated the digital revolution, creating a pressing need for new regulations on digital data flows, and MFA is asked how it works with countries, the UN and ASEAN on international norms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the pandemic has accelerated the digital revolution and its role in driving economic growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Therefore, there is a pressing need for new regulations to ensure the safety and security of digital data flows, such as consumers' personal information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Can MFA share how we are working bilaterally with other countries as well as with platforms like the UN and ASEAN, to develop and strengthen international norms, not only to take digital cooperation forward, but also to ensure that cyberspace remains safe, secure and open for our citizens.

sections.label: Diplomatic neutrality and economic tensions
sections.summary: Singapore's position of diplomatic neutrality must continue, though economically it cannot afford to be indifferent to these tensions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our position of diplomatic neutrality must continue, though economically, we cannot afford to be indifferent to these tensions.

sections.label: Preparing globalised economy for uncertainty
sections.summary: The Government is asked how it is preparing the heavily globalised Singaporean economy to remain resilient amid economic uncertainties businesses, especially SMEs, might face.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Economically, however, we seek updates on how the Government is preparing the heavily globalised Singaporean economy to remain resilient in light of economic uncertainties that businesses, especially SMES might face?

sections.label: Protest deaths and Singapore's position
sections.summary: With protestors reportedly killed by Security Forces, at least 18 yesterday, the Foreign Minister is asked for Singapore's position on the crisis and its role in facilitating a consensus for a meeting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: The death toll of protestors being killed by Security Forces has reportedly been increasing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: And yesterday, it was reported at least 18 have been killed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Given the continued uncertainty and tenseness of developments, will the Foreign Minister provide an update on Singapore's position on the crisis?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Will he also inform the House of Singapore's role in facilitating the emergence of a consensus for a meeting, if there is one, and what we hope can be achieved from this meeting?

sections.label: Myanmar calls to boycott Singapore firms
sections.summary: Calls in Myanmar to boycott Singapore firms began after Dr Balakrishnan's earlier answer included a line on separating business and politics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Calls in Myanmar for the boycotting of Singapore firms began after Dr Balakrishnan's earlier answer to the House which included a line on separating business and politics.

sections.label: Singaporeans in Myanmar extraction plans
sections.summary: Singaporeans in Myanmar should know of contingency plans for extraction should the need arise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: Singaporeans in Myanmar should know of the contingency plans for extraction should the need arise.

sections.label: Causeway travellers before pandemic
sections.summary: Before the pandemic, Causeway travellers between Johor and Singapore averaged over 300,000 daily, over a third Malaysians commuting for work and study.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Prior to the pandemic, travelers using the Causeway between Johor and Singapore averaged over 300,000 per day, with over a third being Malaysians who commute daily for work and study.

sections.label: Singapore and Indonesia economic ties
sections.summary: Singapore's economy contracted 5.08% in 2020 and Indonesia's 2.07%, yet Singapore remained Indonesia's largest foreign investor in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Singapore's economy, contracted by 5.08% in 2020, while Indonesia's contracted by 2.07%.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Nonetheless, Singapore remained Indonesia's largest foreign investor in 2020.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: We also rank among each other's largest trading partners, with Indonesia ranking number 6 amongst Singapore's top trading partners in 2020 and a merchandise value of $48.8 billion.

sections.label: Singapore COVID-19 aid to Brunei
sections.summary: In March 2020, the Singapore Government contributed 3,000 diagnostic tests and one PCR machine to Brunei's COVID-19 fight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In March 2020, the Singapore Government contributed 3,000 diagnostic tests and one PCR machine to support the Brunei Government's fight against COVID-19.

sections.label: RCEP signed at ASEAN
sections.summary: At the ASEAN held on 15 November, the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership or RCEP was signed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: For instance, at the ASEAN held on 15 November, the landmark Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership or RCEP was signed.

sections.label: ASEAN survey US versus China
sections.summary: Six in 10 ASEAN respondents would choose the US over China, with Myanmar, Brunei and Laos favouring China.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: The survey results showed that overall, six in 10 respondents in ASEAN would choose the US over China, if forced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: When broken down by country, survey respondents from three countries should greater support for China, than the US, namely Myanmar, Brunei and Laos, while the respondents from the other seven countries showed stronger support for the US than China.

sections.label: Singapore 2020 investment figures
sections.summary: In 2020 Singapore attracted $17.2 billion in investments despite its worst recession since Independence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In 2020, Singapore attracted Singapore attracted $17.2 billion in investments, despite its worst recession since Independence.

sections.label: DPM Heng three focus areas
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Heng has identified three areas for focus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng has identified three areas for focus.

sections.label: ASEAN connectivity and community vision
sections.summary: ASEAN is an important grouping for Singapore to strengthen connectivity and realise the ASEAN Community by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: From this perspective, ASEAN is an important grouping for Singapore to strengthen our connectivity with Southeast Asia, to deepen our role as a hub for the region and sharing the vision of realising the ASEAN Community by 2025.

sections.label: Relations with ASEAN neighbours
sections.summary: Singapore maintained cordial relations with ASEAN neighbours and cooperated on community-building, smart cities and digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We worked hard to maintain strong and cordial relations with our neighbours in the ASEAN countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We have also been cooperating closely with them to advance ASEAN's community-building efforts and develop new areas of collaboration such as smart cities and digitalisation.

sections.label: Umrah pilgrimages on hold
sections.summary: Umrah pilgrimages are on hold until at least the third quarter of 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Umrah pilgrimages are on hold until at least the third quarter of 2021.

sections.label: Abraham Accords normalise Israel relations
sections.summary: The Abraham Accords normalised relations between Israel and the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Abraham Accords normalised relations between Israel and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) as well as Bahrain.

sections.label: GCC-Singapore Free Trade Agreement
sections.summary: Exchanges exist in sectors including healthcare, governance, culture and the environment, and Singapore is the first country outside the Middle East to conclude an FTA with the GCC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: There are exchanges in a number of sectors, including healthcare, governance, culture and the environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We have the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC)-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (GSFTA) and we are the first country outside of the Middle East to conclude a free trade agreement (FTA) with the GCC.

sections.label: US notice to withdraw from WHO
sections.summary: In July 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, the US administration officially gave notice to withdraw from the World Health Organization.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: In the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic in July 2020, the US administration officially gave notice to withdraw from World Health Organization.

sections.label: US leaves global pact
sections.summary: The United States formally left the global pact on 4 November 2020, the day after the US elections that gave Joe Biden as the 46th American president.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: The United States formally left the global pact on 4 November 2020, which, ironically, was the day after the US elections, which gave us Joe Biden as the 46th American president.

sections.label: Biden signs executive orders
sections.summary: On the first day after his inauguration, Biden signed 15 executive orders, including one to re-join the Paris Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
sentences.text: On the first day after his inauguration, Biden signed 15 executive orders, including one to re-join the Paris Agreement.

sections.label: 16th Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation
sections.summary: In December 2020, both countries came together for the 16th Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In December 2020, both countries came together for the 16th Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation.

sections.label: RCEP and Singapore-China trade
sections.summary: The conclusion of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership is hoped to further invigorate Singapore-China trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The recent conclusion of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP) would hopefully further invigorate Singapore-China trade.

sections.label: Singaporeans living abroad
sections.summary: There are currently 200,000 Singaporeans living abroad.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, there are currently 200,000 Singaporeans living abroad.

sections.label: Foreign direct investment and Singaporeans
sections.summary: Singapore is the fifth largest recipient of foreign direct investment inflows, so external developments affect every Singaporean's future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Furthermore, with Singapore as the fifth largest recipient of foreign direct investment inflows in the world, external developments will have a marked bearing on the future of every Singaporean.

sections.label: Hub status under threat
sections.summary: Singapore's status as an air, maritime and financial hub is threatened by uncertainty, travel restrictions and tighter border controls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Our status as a hub – air hub, maritime hub, financial hub and more – is being threatened by uncertainty, travel restrictions and tighter border controls.

sections.label: Daren Tang WIPO election
sections.summary: Last year, Singaporean Mr Daren Tang was elected as a Secretary-General of the World Intellectual Property Organization.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Last year, we achieved another milestone in having a Singaporean, Mr Daren Tang, elected as a Secretary-General of the World Intellectual Property Organization.

sections.label: MFA desk officers and embassies
sections.summary: In MFA, about eight desk officers cover about a hundred countries in these regions, with only three resident embassies there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In MFA, there are about eight desk officers who cover about a hundred countries in these regions and only three resident embassies in these regions.

sections.label: Foreign service officers during pandemic
sections.summary: FSOs provided consular support to Singaporeans overseas and remained abroad protecting Singapore's interests during the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: When the pandemic broke, our FSOs played a critical role in providing consular support and comfort to Singaporeans overseas, helping to bring many of them home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the pandemic grew more widespread, our FSOs remained overseas, many in countries where the pandemic was raging and in which it was unsafe for them to remain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They continue to be there now, protecting and advancing Singapore’s interests.

sections.label: Question on FSO COVID-19 protection
sections.summary: A question asks the Minister for Foreign Affairs what measures protect foreign service officers against COVID-19 and plans for their vaccination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this connection, Sir, I would like to ask the Minister for Foreign Affairs what are the measures being taken at missions to protect our foreign service officers against COVID-19 and what are the plans for them as regards getting vaccinated against COVID-19?

sections.label: Largest consular operation bringing Singaporeans home
sections.summary: MFA undertook its largest consular operation, bringing back over 4,500 Singaporeans and their family members.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: At MFA, we undertook our largest ever consular operation in our history.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Mr Alex Yam would know that we worked round the clock and have brought back so far, over 4,500 Singaporeans and their family members.

sections.label: Reuniting Singaporeans from Malaysia
sections.summary: MFA worked with Malaysian authorities to help over 350 elderly, minor or disabled Singaporeans reunite with families in Singapore during border closures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Across the Causeway, we have been working closely with the Malaysian authorities to help more than 350 Singaporeans who are elderly, or minors, or people with disabilities, so that they could reunite with their families in Singapore throughout these border closures.

sections.label: Air freight partnership with New Zealand
sections.summary: An air freight connectivity partnership with New Zealand transported food to Singapore and medical supplies to New Zealand.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And this was absolutely crucial in that time of disruption and upheaval.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We established an air freight connectivity partnership with New Zealand, where flights transported food from New Zealand to Singapore and medical supplies Singapore to New Zealand.

sections.label: Signing RCEP amid nationalism
sections.summary: Signing the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership last year boosted trade and affirmed the importance of multilateral trade relationships.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Nationalism, protectionism, became politically attractive in many parts of the world, especially when there is fear and uncertainty.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: So, the fact that we were still able to sign the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, or RCEP, last year, was an important boost for trade and economic integration but also a statement and affirmation in itself, of the importance of maintaining multilateral trade relationships.

sections.label: Singapore negotiating safe travel arrangements
sections.summary: Singapore is facilitating its economic recovery by continuing to negotiate reciprocal green lanes and other safe travel arrangements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Even now, we are facilitating Singapore's economic recovery by continuing to negotiate reciprocal green lanes, RGLs, and other safe travel arrangements.

sections.label: Singapore and COVAX establishment
sections.summary: Singapore played a key role in establishing the COVAX collective vaccine purchase mechanism, which several Members asked about.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Singapore also played a key role in establishing the COVAX collective vaccine purchase mechanism, which I believe several Members – Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Chong Kee Hiong – have asked about this.

sections.label: Singapore early COVAX supporter
sections.summary: Singapore was an early supporter of the COVAX Facility, which seeks to harmonise public and private incentives for global vaccine development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: No matter how well we control the pandemic within our borders, life cannot resume and get back to the status quo ante, unless the rest of the world is also made safer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This is why Singapore was an early supporter of the COVAX Facility, which seeks to harmonise public and private incentives for global vaccine development.

sections.label: COVAX vaccine allocation
sections.summary: Under COVAX, self-funded countries like Singapore get a small allocation, while subsidised vaccines go to 92 low- and lower middle income countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Under the COVAX mechanism, self-funded countries like Singapore will be allocated a certain small amount.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But really, what this facility does is to ensure that subsidised vaccines will be allocated to other 92 low- and lower middle income countries.

sections.label: Singapore contribution to COVAX
sections.summary: Singapore contributed US$5 million to COVAX to help low-income countries access vaccines through the facility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: He used it in June last year and it has since been acknowledged by the WHO Director General, and it has entered the international anti-COVID lexicon.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We also contributed US$5 million to COVAX to help low-income countries access vaccines through this facility.

sections.label: Digital Economy Agreements concluded
sections.summary: Singapore concluded Digital Economy Agreements with Australia, Chile and New Zealand and is exploring more with other partners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: To sustain growth and help us move ahead in the digital economy, we need to develop common frameworks, common global standards to ensure that cross-border transactions and engagements and digital exchanges, including e-payments and data flows, are safe, secure and efficient.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This is why we concluded Digital Economy Agreements with Australia, Chile and New Zealand, and are exploring more with other partners.

sections.label: Rising global debt overhang
sections.summary: Global debt was already rising at unprecedented post-financial crisis levels, and COVID-19 doubled the global debt overhang.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: First, global debt is already rising at unprecedented levels in the post-financial crisis era, that was 2007, 2008.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Now, with COVID-19, you have seen a doubling of the global debt overhang.

sections.label: US-China relations downward spiral
sections.summary: COVID-19 has accelerated the pre-existing downward spiral of US-China relations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The third risk that we are going to confront is that COVID-19 has, in fact, accelerated the pre-existing downward spiral of the US-China relations.

sections.label: Tariffs against China likely remain
sections.summary: Even with the new Biden administration, measures and tariffs against China are unlikely to be removed in the near future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Even with new Biden administration, it is unlikely that the measures and tariffs against China will be removed in the near future.

sections.label: Halt violence and lethal force
sections.summary: The immediate priority is to halt all acts of violence and lethal force and step back from a deteriorating situation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The immediate priority is to halt all acts of violence and the use of lethal force and to step back from a rapidly deteriorating situation.

sections.label: Myanmar military restraint and detainee release
sections.summary: It calls on Myanmar's military to exercise restraint, de-escalate, negotiate in good faith, and immediately release Win Myint, Aung San Suu Kyi and other detainees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We strongly reiterate that the use of lethal weapons against unarmed civilians is inexcusable under all circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We call on the Myanmar military authorities to exercise the utmost restraint, to desist from the use of lethal force and to take immediate steps to de-escalate the situation in order to prevent further bloodshed, violence and deaths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We therefore call on all parties in Myanmar to engage in discussions and to negotiate in good faith, to pursue long-term peaceful political solutions for them to achieve national reconciliation, including a path to find a way to get back to the path of democratic transition.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And we believe this can only begin if President Win Myint, and State Counsellor and Foreign Minister Aung San Suu Ky and the other detainees are immediately released.

sections.label: Special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting
sections.summary: A special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting will be convened by video conference tomorrow to listen to the Myanmar military authorities' representative.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: A special ASEAN Foreign Ministers' Meeting will be convened via video conference tomorrow and where we will listen to the representative of the Myanmar military authorities.

sections.label: ASEAN economic integration cooperation
sections.summary: The passage states it is imperative to press on with economic integration, fulfil ASEAN Community Blueprints and expand cooperation with external partners inclusively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Accelerated no doubt by COVID-19 but really, fundamental trends that were already there beforehand.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And so, it is imperative that we press on with economic integration, fulfil the ASEAN Community Blueprints, and continue to expand cooperation with all of ASEAN's external partners in an inclusive way.

sections.label: US FDI in Southeast Asia
sections.summary: US foreign direct investment stock in Southeast Asia exceeds US$338 billion, more than US investment in India, Japan, South Korea and China combined.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The cumulative stock of US foreign direct investment (FDI) in Southeast Asia stands at more than US$338 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: What is more important is that this sum is more than what the US has invested in India, Japan, South Korea and China combined.

sections.label: US investments in Singapore
sections.summary: About 85% of total US investments in Southeast Asia are in Singapore, which creates many good jobs there.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Approximately 85% of the US total investments in Southeast Asia are in Singapore – which creates many good jobs here.

sections.label: China trade and investment ties
sections.summary: China remains Singapore's largest trading partner and Singapore is China's largest foreign investor.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: China remains our largest trading partner, and surprisingly, we are China's largest foreign investor.

sections.label: China reciprocal agreement trust
sections.summary: China was the first country with which Singapore established a reciprocal agreement, due to pandemic control and a large reservoir of trust.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: That is how you prove that you are a reliable partner, when a crisis breaks out and the chips are down.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Therefore, you should not be surprised that China was the first country with which we established a reciprocal agreement – both because we have both been able to control the pandemic domestically and also because of this large reservoir of trust.

sections.label: Reciprocal Green Lane suspension
sections.summary: The Reciprocal Green Lane and Periodic Commuting Arrangement launched 10 August 2020; the Green Lane was suspended three months from 1 February 2021 and will be reviewed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Shortly after, we launched the Reciprocal Green Lane (RGL) and the Periodic Commuting Arrangement on 10 August 2020 for essential work, business and official travel.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Given the resurgence of COVID-19 worldwide, including in Malaysia in recent months, we had to suspend the Reciprocal Green Lane for three months from 1 February 2021 but we will review this after the suspension period.

sections.label: RTS Link Project negotiations
sections.summary: Negotiations to resume the Rapid Transit System Link Project were concluded in July last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: For example, we concluded negotiations to resume the Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link Project in July last year.

sections.label: High Speed Rail agreement termination
sections.summary: Malaysia let the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail Bilateral Agreement be terminated on 31 December 2020 and agreed to compensate Singapore for costs incurred.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: For example, Malaysia allowed the Kuala Lumpur-Singapore High Speed Rail (HSR) Bilateral Agreement (BA) to be terminated on 31 December 2020 and has agreed to compensate Singapore for costs already incurred by Singapore in fulfilling our obligations under the HSR BA in accordance with this agreement.

sections.label: Singapore-Indonesia Leaders' Retreat framework
sections.summary: At the last Singapore-Indonesia Leaders' Retreat, Prime Minister Lee and President Jokowi welcomed the agreed Framework for Discussions, where military training and the Flight Information Region will be discussed separately but concurrently.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: At the last Singapore-Indonesia Leaders' Retreat, Prime Minister Lee and President Jokowi also welcomed our agreed "Framework for Discussions", where military training and the Flight Information Region (FIR) will be discussed separately but concurrently.

sections.label: Looking ahead at foreign uncertainty
sections.summary: Looking ahead, uncertainty on the foreign horizon remains, but the last year showed Singapore's resilience, preserved relevance and strengthened reputation as a principled, reliable and credible actor.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, as we look ahead, there is much uncertainty on the horizon, particularly the foreign horizon.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: There will continue to be unexpected currents, gales, typhoons, maybe even tsunamis that could potentially throw us off course.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But the last year has shown that – as Singapore Inc, as the Singapore people and the ship of Singapore – we have demonstrated our resilience as a people and as a country.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have made sacrifices for each other, we have looked out for each other's well-being and safety, we have kept the public health situation under control, and leaving no Singaporean behind anywhere in the world has been perhaps the best reminder about the value of citizenship.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: It is not just a red passport opening doors all over the rest of the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have preserved our relevance and I think we have actually strengthened our reputation as a principled, reliable and credible actor on the international stage.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: These will stand us in good stead going forward as we continue to pursue Singapore's long-term interests, always preserving our independence and our unique identity as a multi-racial, multicultural city state in the heart of Southeast Asia.

sections.label: COVID-19 external environment disruptions
sections.summary: COVID-19 has caused major disruptions in Singapore's external environment.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: COVID-19 has caused major disruptions in our external environment.

sections.label: Singapore largest Indonesia investor 2020
sections.summary: Singapore remained Indonesia's largest foreign investor in 2020, a position held since 2014, with investments increasing by 50% over 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore remained Indonesia’s largest foreign investor in 2020, a position we have held since 2014.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In fact, Singapore’s investments in Indonesia increased by 50% in 2020 over 2019.

sections.label: Singapore-Malaysia COVID-19 cooperation
sections.summary: Singapore and Malaysia are second-largest trading partners, and after Malaysia's March 2020 MCO, a Special Working Committee on COVID-19 was formed.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore and Malaysia are each other’s second-largest trading partners and significant investors.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: On 18 March 2020, Malaysia imposed its first Movement Control Order (MCO).

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We immediately formed the Singapore-Malaysia Special Working Committee on COVID-19 to ensure both sides could work together and achieve a mutually beneficial outcome as well as facilitate the safe movement of essential people, goods and services.

sections.label: Singapore investment in Batam
sections.summary: Singapore invested US$132 million in Batam in the first three quarters of 2020 and funded 620 projects there.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Many of these opportunities are currently situated in the Province of Riau Islands (KEPRI), specifically Batam, where investment from Singapore totaled US$132 million in the first three quarters of 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore was also the country that invested in the largest number of projects in Batam, with investments in a total of 620 projects.

sections.label: Six Bilateral Economic Working Groups meeting
sections.summary: The 6WG Ministerial Meeting was held virtually to advance projects like Kendal Industrial Park and increase agricultural trade.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We have continued to maintain strong momentum on our bilateral economic projects.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We convened the Six Bilateral Economic Working Groups (6WG) Ministerial Meeting virtually, allowing us to advance mutually beneficial projects such as the Kendal Industrial Park and exploring ways to increase the volume of trade in agricultural products.

sections.label: Singapore-Indonesia Reciprocal Green Lane
sections.summary: The Singapore-Indonesia Reciprocal Green Lane was launched in October 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In addition, we launched the Singapore-Indonesia Reciprocal Green Lane (RGL) in October 2020.

sections.label: Masks and sanitisers to Indonesia
sections.summary: In November last year, 10 million surgical masks and two million bottles of hand sanitisers were delivered to Indonesian provinces and organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In November last year, we arranged for the delivery of 10 million surgical masks and two million bottles of hand sanitisers to Indonesian provinces and organisations.

sections.label: RCEP signing in November 2020
sections.summary: The RCEP was signed in November 2020 and will eliminate tariffs for about 92% of goods traded among members.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The historic signing of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership, or RCEP, in November 2020 is a positive development amidst difficult times.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: It will boost confidence in regional trade and investment, with the elimination of tariffs for about 92% of goods on average traded among members.

sections.label: ASEAN Code of Conduct talks
sections.summary: The COC is a key ASEAN-led process for managing South China Sea disputes, with second reading of the Single Draft Negotiating Text begun in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: A key ASEAN-led process to manage the SCS disputes is the Code of Conduct, or COC, in the SCS negotiations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We have made good progress and commenced the second reading of the Single Draft Negotiating Text in 2019.

sections.label: Singapore contribution to ASEAN Fund
sections.summary: Singapore contributed US$100,000 to the Fund to buy medical equipment and other items helping ASEAN member states combat the pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore contributed US$100,000 to the Fund which will be used to purchase medical equipment and other items to help fellow ASEAN member states combat the pandemic.

sections.label: Indian investments in Singapore
sections.summary: Indian investments in Singapore rose from S$21.9 billion in 2009 to S$28.8 billion in 2019 in finance, insurance and ICT.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Likewise, Indian investments in Singapore have increased from S$21.9 billion in 2009 to S$28.8 billion in 2019 in sectors such as finance, insurance and information communications technology or ICT.

sections.label: Singapore-Saudi Joint Committee
sections.summary: Singapore is establishing a Singapore-Saudi Joint Committee on economic cooperation, mooted during President Halimah Yacob's November 2019 State Visit to Saudi Arabia.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: At the G-to-G level, we seek to enhance economic and political collaboration with key partners where opportune.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We are in the midst of establishing the Singapore-Saudi Joint Committee on economic cooperation, mooted during President Halimah Yacob’s State Visit to Saudi Arabia in November 2019.

sections.label: African Continental Free Trade Agreement
sections.summary: The AfCFTA launched in January 2021 may create opportunities for businesses in a market of over 1.2 billion people with US$3.4 trillion combined GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: The launch of the African Continental Free Trade Agreement (AfCFTA) in January 2021 may well create opportunities for our businesses to tap into a market of over 1.2 billion people, with a combined GDP of US$3.4 trillion.

sections.label: Kenya customs clearance time
sections.summary: In Kenya, it helped customs agencies cut bonded cargo clearance time from Mombasa to Malaba from 20 days to under three days.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In Kenya, it has helped customs agencies reduce the time taken to clear bonded cargo travelling from Mombasa to Malaba from 20 days to under three days.

sections.label: Digital Economy Partnership Agreement signed
sections.summary: Singapore signed the Digital Economy Partnership Agreement with Chile and New Zealand in June 2020, establishing new digital trade approaches and collaborations.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore also signed the Digital Economy Partnership Agreement with Chile and New Zealand in June 2020, a first of its kind agreement that establishes new approaches and collaborations in digital trade, promotes interoperability and addresses new issues brought about by digitalisation.

sections.label: FTA talks with Pacific Alliance
sections.summary: Last year, FTA negotiations with the Pacific Alliance, comprising Chile, Colombia, Mexico and Peru, reached substantial conclusion in December.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Last year, we made good progress with the substantial conclusion of the FTA negotiations with the Pacific Alliance, which comprises Chile, Colombia, Mexico and Peru in December.

sections.label: MERCOSUR market size and GDP
sections.summary: MERCOSUR represents a market of 266 million people and a combined GDP of US$4.44 trillion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: MERCOSUR represents a market of 266 million people and a combined GDP of US$4.44 trillion.

sections.label: US economic and defence partner
sections.summary: The US is a major economic and defence partner for Singapore and its largest source of FDI.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):    The US is a major economic and defence partner for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: It is also our largest source of FDI.

sections.label: Provincial business councils and RCEP
sections.summary: Eight provincial business councils support Singapore companies in China and RCEP signing shows commitment to economic integration and new opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Our eight provincial business councils allow us to support Singapore companies to participate in China’s economic transformation; promote the internationalisation of Chinese enterprises through Singapore as a regional hub; and deepen collaboration in new areas such as connectivity, sustainability, and modern services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The signing of the RCEP is a strong testament of the region’s commitment to deepening economic integration despite challenging times.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: It will boost confidence in trade and investment and open up new business opportunities with RCEP economies, including China.

sections.label: Sharing development through Singapore Cooperation Programme
sections.summary: It is in Singapore's interest for the region to grow, and it shares development experiences through the Singapore Cooperation Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: It is therefore in our interest for our region to grow and prosper.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We have been proactively sharing our development experiences and know-how in areas where we can contribute, for example, though the Singapore Cooperation Programme.

sections.label: Repatriation of stranded Singaporeans
sections.summary: MFA and other agencies ran repatriation operations, reuniting over 350 children with parents in Singapore and helping overseas Singaporeans return home.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: To facilitate their return, MFA officers, together with ICA, MOH, MOT and LTA, worked tirelessly and they launched several repatriation operations to reunite over 350 children with their parents in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Our overseas Missions also worked around the clock with airlines and foreign authorities to facilitate safe passage home for overseas Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: We have also worked with our network of Honorary Consuls around the world to extend our consular presence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Our Honorary Consul-General (HCG) in Lima Mr Winston Merchor helped with the repatriation of 14 Singaporeans and their families who were stranded in Peru last year.

sections.label: MFA officers staying at posts
sections.summary: MFA will protect its frontline officers, and no MFA officer asked to leave his or her post to come home.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: MFA will also protect our officers on the frontlines, and I thank Mr Raj Joshua Thomas for raising this.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Even as the global health situation deteriorated, not a single MFA officer, not one, not a single one, has asked to leave his or her post to come home.

sections.label: Standing ground in foreign policy
sections.summary: An issue will arise requiring Singapore to stand its ground and say no, testing unity, cohesion and support of its own people.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The fundamental fact is this: we will be pushed and pulled.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But whenever you are in a sweet spot, always anticipate that things can only go downhill from there.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: So, I am sure, sooner rather than later, an issue will arise and we will have to stand our ground.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We will have to say no and it will be a test of our unity and our cohesion; and as the Member has quite rightly identified, our understanding and support of our own people because foreign policy begins at home.

sections.label: Long-term interests of Singapore
sections.summary: MFA, the Prime Minister and the entire Cabinet will always make decisions based on Singapore's long-term interests.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And it can come from either or from both sides.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But rest assured that MFA, indeed the Prime Minister and the entire Cabinet, will always make decisions on the basis of the long-term interests of Singapore.

sections.label: COVAX donation to WHO
sections.summary: A question asks whether Singapore requested the WHO to earmark its net COVAX donation to ASEAN countries or left it for general distribution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: The first question is, he earlier said that Singapore is a net donor to the COVAX programme and I wonder whether he could tell us whether we have actually made a request to the WHO to earmark our net donation to ASEAN countries, or have we made a decision to leave it open for general distribution by WHO?

sections.label: COVAX risk pooling concept
sections.summary: Ascertaining long-term vaccine efficacy and safety takes a long time, so the concept behind COVAX is risk pooling.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: And in any case, it would take a long time, by definition, to ascertain the long-term efficacy and safety of vaccines.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Therefore, the concept behind COVAX is risk pooling.

sections.label: Advance market commitments structure
sections.summary: Countries with more resources, including Singapore, would make advance market commitments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The way it was structured was that countries with more resources, and that included Singapore, would make advance market commitments.

sections.label: US$5 million COVID-19 help
sections.summary: Singapore put in US$5 million to help other parts of the world avoid becoming endemic reservoirs for further mutations.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But apart from doing that, to also express our willingness to help other parts of the world whom if we did not help, would become endemic reservoirs for further mutations and for this never-ending curse of COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: That is why we put US$5 million into this.

sections.label: Singapore vaccine decisions science
sections.summary: Singapore will make decisions on vaccines on the basis of science and healthcare needs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: As to vaccine power play, I do not want to get into the details of that.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: But I do want to make one point which I think is salient for our local population and it is this: Singapore will make decisions on vaccines on the basis of science and healthcare needs.

sections.label: MFA role and amendment withdrawal
sections.summary: MFA plays a crucial role ensuring Singapore is not crushed as elephants roam, and the amendment is withdrawn.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Chairman, Mr Lee Kuan Yew in 1973 said that when "the elephants fight or flirt, the grass suffers and when they make love, it is disastrous".

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Our MFA plays crucial role in ensuring that we are not crushed as elephants roam about us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Chairman, I therefore beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
